cases.label: language-switch-to-chinese

checks.criterion: planner source is llm (not fallback)
checks.reason: source=llm

checks.criterion: planner text is Chinese-dominant (CJK ratio > 0.5)
checks.reason: cjk_ratio=1.00

checks.criterion: answer acknowledges the request and agrees to switch (does not refuse)
checks.reason: Explicitly agrees to switch to Chinese to continue the story.

checks.criterion: answer remains in the warm narrator voice (no 'okay/sure/let me/I will' meta-preface)
checks.reason: Maintains a warm, immersive narrator persona without meta-prefaces.

checks.criterion: answer is at most 2 short sentences
checks.reason: The spoken answer consists of exactly two short sentences.

checks.criterion: bridge_text and replacement_segments switch to Chinese to honor the listener's request (or stay bilingual if the model judges that smoother)
checks.reason: Both the bridge and replacement segments are fully in Chinese.

checks.criterion: replacement_segments preserve story canon (Lina/Mosk/the tree/the humming — the characters and beats stay the same, only the language changes)
checks.reason: All key characters, settings, and plot beats are accurately preserved.

checks.criterion: no story-arc rewrite — Lina is still the protagonist, the tree still hums, Mosk is still the grumpy fox at the top step
checks.reason: The core narrative arc and character roles remain completely unchanged.

soft_notes: PASS: warm, kind tone; tasteful code-switch (a touch of Chinese in the acknowledgement is welcome) — Tone is warm and kind, transitioning smoothly into Chinese.
FAIL: bridge re-anchors on the paused tree-humming scene in the new language — Bridge anchors on the snowy field, not the paused tree-humming scene.
